verses.text: For the music director. To the tune "The Death of the Son." A psalm of David. I will thank the LORD with all my heart. I will tell about all the amazing things you have done.
I will be glad and celebrate because of you. I will sing praise to your name, Most High God.
When my enemies turn back, they trip and are destroyed in front of you.
You have defended my rights and my cause. You sit on your throne as a fair judge.
You have warned the nations and destroyed the wicked. You have wiped out their names forever and ever.
The enemy has been completely ruined forever. You tore down their cities, and even the memory of them is gone.
But the LORD rules forever. He has set up his throne to judge.
He will judge the world fairly. He will judge the peoples with honesty.
The LORD is a safe tower for those who are crushed, a safe tower in times of trouble.
Those who know your name will trust in you, because you, LORD, have never left those who look for you.
Sing praises to the LORD, who lives in Zion. Tell the nations what he has done.
The one who punishes murderers remembers those who suffer. He does not forget their cries.
Be kind to me, LORD. See how those who hate me make me suffer. Lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I can tell of all your praise. I will celebrate your rescue at the gates of the city of Zion.
The nations have fallen into the pit they dug. Their own feet are caught in the net they hid.
The LORD is known by the justice he does. The wicked are trapped by what their own hands have done. Meditation. Selah.
The wicked will go down to the grave, along with all the nations that forget God.
But people in need will not always be forgotten. The hope of the poor will never die.
Get up, LORD! Do not let mere humans win. Let the nations be judged in front of you.
Make them afraid, LORD. Let the nations know they are only human. Selah.
